local_metadata_raw.title: A qualitative pre-Schwarzian improvement for real schlicht functions
local_metadata_raw.description: For normalized univalent functions with real Taylor coefficients, the classical centered pre-Schwarzian disk can be strictly shrunk at every fixed nonreal point, uniformly over the class. Its radius remains sharp on the real diameter. This research note gives a qualitative answer to Hayman–Lingham Problem 6.86 using classical second-coefficient equality, reflection symmetry of the equality domains, and compactness. The gap is uniform on compact nonreal sets. Real disk automorphisms reduce the unknown sharp radius to one variable, and exact examples give lower bounds and two limiting obstructions to a global positive gap. No explicit upper-gap formula, sharp numerical radius, general extremizer or full variability region is determined. No new general method, historical firstness, exhaustive novelty clearance or current-openness guarantee is claimed. The bounded priority audit retains unresolved original-source limits for Jenkins (1960) and Aleksandrov–Popova (1973). Related earlier linear extreme-point and argument estimates are distinguished from the nonlinear derivative quotient. The verification archive preserves the original candidate and controlling scope note, independent analytic/source and priority audits, exact algebraic controls, and explicitly uncertified numerical replays; full third-party source scans are excluded. AI tools were used extensively in development, verification, source investigation and writing. This is an unrefereed preprint; internal AI reviews do not constitute human peer review.
